A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ReFlow study, and their main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison. Several v2 appendix captions are visually clipped, but their text is recoverable and the corresponding figures can be matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on three fluid-flow benchmarks, including statistical accuracy, computational efficiency, and trajectory analyses in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds original integrator comparisons and adaptive-sampler sensitivity results in Section 7.

M1.justification: v2 introduces a curvature-aware inference procedure using an EMA velocity-deviation proxy, velocity blending, and adaptive step sizes (Equations 5–7). This substantially extends v1's generic ODE sampling procedure, while retaining the basic training objective and network architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate cloud–shock, shear-layer, and Richtmyer–Meshkov flows under the retained distribution settings. The new sampler study uses ShearLayer2D. References to additional benchmarks and OOD regimes do not supply identifiable new coverage in the appendices.

E2.justification: The four surrogate baselines remain unchanged in the main benchmark comparison. However, Tables 2–4 add a substantial numerical-sampler comparison against the built-in sampler, torchdiffeq Midpoint, Euler, RK2, and RK4 to evaluate the new adaptive controller.

E3.justification: Section 7 adds a frozen-model sampling evaluation using 10 macros × 20 micros, relative L2 error, neural function evaluations, and their Cost×Err product. This is an additional protocol; the earlier 10 × 1,000 macro–micro benchmark specification remains in Appendix K.

E4.justification: v2 adds controlled integrator comparisons and a 20-configuration controller sensitivity study, varying EMA, blending, gating, damping, calibration, and an orthogonal-filter option. The earlier training-efficiency, PCA, trajectory, and spectral analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Tables 2 and 3 newly report relative L2 errors as mean ± standard deviation. The standard deviation's aggregation level is not clearly specified, and no repeated-training run counts or random-seed reporting are added.

E6.justification: The main benchmark values and training-efficiency table are unchanged (Table 5.1 → Table 1; Table D.1 → Table 7). Tables 2–4 add substantial sampler results: within the new study, Euler-16 reports 0.2489 relative L2 error at 16 evaluations, versus 0.2369 at 10.7 average evaluations for ema_0.25.

T1.justification: v2 expands v1's coupling and velocity formulation into extensive formal analysis in Sections 4–5 and Appendices A–I. Additions include exact transport, terminal-error decomposition, Euler discretization bounds, an EMA lemma, spectral-capacity and structure-function results, and combined law-level error bounds.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution list now present law-level theoretical guarantees and curvature-aware integration as central contributions. This substantially broadens v1's emphasis on adapting rectified flow for efficient fluid sampling, while retaining the principal statistical-fidelity and speed claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds interpretations linking spectral tails to resolution limits and separating coverage, fit, straightness, and discretization errors. It also distinguishes marginal W1 evaluation from field-law W2 analysis and introduces explanations of controller robustness, fixed-step brittleness, and conditional diversity.

D1.justification: v2 adds sampler-configuration values and identifies the torchdiffeq reference implementation. Appendix O newly promises datasets, processing scripts, a training/evaluation pipeline, and a checkpoint before acceptance, but supplies no access link. Existing architecture, training, preprocessing, and hardware disclosures are largely unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 explicitly connects the work to Lanthaler et al.'s statistical-solution and correlation framework and removes the Bartolucci, Raonic, and Mousavi operator references. The diffusion-related-work discussion remains largely unchanged; Lanthaler 2021a and 2021b duplicate the same previously cited work.

P1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and mathematical exposition are substantially rewritten around a law-level narrative. Method and implementation sections are reorganized, and the supplementary material is restructured with a theory appendix replacing the earlier contents-led opening. Much experimental prose remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds three sampler tables and extensively changes typography, table styling, and figure sizing and placement. Existing plots are largely reused, but several Appendix P captions now fall partly or entirely outside the visible page, including Figures 19–20 and 24.

improvement.justification: Tables 2–4 add useful controlled comparisons and sensitivity evidence, but new theoretical and reporting defects counterbalance these gains. Lemma E.3's EMA bound contradicts its recurrence: for lambda=0.75, v0=0 and v1=1, the deviation is 0.75 while the stated bound is 0.25. Section 7 also promises supplementary integrator tables and Pareto plots that are absent, and several captions are newly clipped. With the original benchmark results unchanged, these tradeoffs prevent a reliable net quality judgment.
